payload.alternatives: Every satellite now, empty ones included: more repositories to keep (CI, Dependabot, security) with nothing in them. Only the monorepo: the presentation pages would wait for a product release. The packages split into repositories of their own: lockstep releases across repositories, and the two readers no longer held in one commit.
payload.rationale: The packages release in lockstep (one version across the nine manifests), depend on each other through workspace:*, the format and both readers (TypeScript and Python) change in one commit, and the required guards read across packages (the packed tarball, the command roster, the host contract, the built-in stack index). Split, each change of format would become a cascade of releases, and the two readers could drift with nobody seeing it. The site and the organization's profile have a cadence of their own; a Marketplace listing for the Action (action.yml at a repository's root) and a Homebrew tap (a homebrew-* repository) are a platform's demand. An empty repository is one more place to keep (CI, Dependabot, security) and nobody else can take a name inside the organization, so none is made ahead of its content.
payload.title: The mnema-work organization holds the product in one repository, mnema, transferred from felipesauer/mnema with its history, and a satellite repository is born only when its lifecycle, release cadence or a platform demand differs from the product, never for tidiness: mnema.work (the site) and .github (the organization profile and default community files) now, action and homebrew-mnema when there is something to put in them; mnema stays the central reference

payload.alternatives: The site stays in the monorepo: one source, but every presentation change waits for the required checks and a release. The docs moved into the site repository: separated from the commands they describe and from the guards that hold them. The release dispatching the site build: a token between repositories.
payload.rationale: Today the site deploys only from a release (site.yml), which is right for the docs, which describe the version npm serves, and wrong for presentation pages, where fixing one sentence would wait for a product release and its 25 required checks. The docs stay where the commands they describe and the guards that hold them live; the site repository takes them from the latest release tag, so the rule that the docs describe the published version holds. A scheduled check of the latest tag instead of a dispatch from the release keeps any token out of both repositories. What the split costs, a docs change that breaks the site build seen only at the next build, is closed by the light check in the product repository.
payload.title: The site moves to its own repository, mnema-work/mnema.work: it holds the presentation pages and the build, deploys its own pages on a push, and builds the docs from docs/ of the latest release tag of mnema, found by a scheduled check so that no token crosses repositories; the docs stay authored in the product repository, where a light check keeps building the docs pages on each pull request; the deploy job keeps holding no secret and running no checkout

payload.alternatives: The apex without the redirect: every homepage already published on npm, the extension and the plugins would answer 404. www as the canonical address: one more hop for the address people type, nothing gained.
payload.rationale: mnema.work is the project's own domain. GitHub Pages does not redirect a transferred repository's site, and npm 0.1.0 to 0.1.5, the VS Code extension and the plugins published felipesauer.github.io/mnema/ as their homepage, which cannot be changed on what is published; once the repository leaves the personal account that path is served by the maintainer's user site, so a page-for-page redirect there keeps every one of them working. The paths map one to one (/mnema/docs/<page> to /docs/<page>). Cloudflare's proxy would stop GitHub from issuing the certificate, so the records stay DNS only. The search engines' verification and the robots file move to mnema.work; the rest of 01a188d1 (titles, descriptions, canonicals, structured data, sitemap) stands.
payload.title: The site is read at https://mnema.work (the presentation), /docs/<page> (the docs of the published version) and /record/ (the record verifier); www redirects to the apex and the DNS records stay DNS only so GitHub issues the certificate; the old address felipesauer.github.io/mnema/ is kept alive by a page-for-page redirect in the maintainer user site, and the search engines are verified on mnema.work

payload.alternatives: work.mnema/mnema by DNS authentication: the brand name, but a private key held as a secret in the npm environment. Keeping io.github.felipesauer/mnema: a workflow in the organization repository is granted the organization namespace, not the old owner one.
payload.rationale: mcp-publisher login github-oidc grants the namespace of the repository's owner: from mnema-work/mnema the workflow is granted io.github.mnema-work/*, and io.github.felipesauer/mnema can no longer be published from it. Keeping OIDC keeps the property the release has today, that no job holds a registry secret. The name changes in server.json, the generator of server.json, the package's mcpName and the release's checks in the same pull request.
payload.title: From the first release after the move, mnema is listed in the official MCP Registry as io.github.mnema-work/mnema, published by the release workflow through GitHub OIDC as before, so the release keeps holding no secret; io.github.felipesauer/mnema stays at 0.1.5 and is marked as replaced where the registry allows it

payload.alternatives: Keeping the two secrets: forgotten credentials that travel with the transfer. Two-factor not required: nothing gained now, and every later member or outside collaborator would join without it. Keeping Mnema AI as the display name: not the brand.
payload.rationale: The organization has one member today, and requiring two-factor authentication costs nothing now and covers every member and outside collaborator later. Its display name follows the brand. The repository secrets NPM_TOKEN and RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN are read by no workflow (npm publishes by trusted publishing, without a token): forgotten credentials that would travel with the transfer; their names, never their values, are kept in the phase 1 snapshot before they go.
payload.title: The mnema-work organization requires two-factor authentication of its members, its display name is Mnema, and the two repository secrets no workflow reads (NPM_TOKEN, RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN) are deleted once the pre-transfer snapshot lists their names

A security address on the project's own domain gives a reporter without a GitHub account a way in; answering by e-mail from the forwarded inbox would send the maintainer's personal address to the reporter, which ADR-167 forbids, so the conversation continues in GitHub's private vulnerability reporting, already on for the repository. The destination inbox is named nowhere in the repository, the site or the record.

payload.alternatives: Raise the timeout to 180 and keep 10 runs: N=30 per night, but nine runners held about 2.5 hours every morning and the pull requests' CI queued behind them. Only Node 24 with 10 runs: loses the comparison between the floor, 24 and 26 that the three Nodes exist for. Turn the night off until the suite is faster: no flake measured meanwhile.
payload.rationale: One run of the suite takes 13.6 minutes on a runner (757 test files, measured on 2026-11-06), so 10 runs per job (about 136 minutes) cannot fit the 90-minute limit and every night since 2026-10-21 was cancelled without a word; 5 runs take about 70 minutes, leaving a margin of 20. A cancelled night opened no issue, which is why seventeen dead nights went unseen. In the organization the free plan shares its runners, and the cron fires hours late (10 to 14 UTC), so a long night holds nine runners during the maintainer's working morning.
payload.title: The flake sampler fits its time limit: a night runs the suite 5 times per job (3 Nodes x 3 shards, N=15 per Node per night), a pull request that touches the sampler runs it once per job to prove it counts, and a night whose ruler breaks (a shard that did not report) opens an issue

payload.alternatives: A memory of what the key signed in the home directory: an agent running as the same user edits it; Signing only what this process appended: with a bound it does not close the hole, without one a crash leaves events unsigned forever; Anchoring in git: does not cover what is not committed nor the private and global trees, and costs a git call per write
payload.rationale: A history rewritten without the key was signed by the holder's next write and then passed --require signed in both readers (audit T-11, reproduced on 0.1.7 and main, and in two more forms: a forged torn end, and content edited with the link hashes kept); this design closed every form in two adversarial reviews (proposal and review in the 2026-11-10 T-11 design)
payload.title: A writer signs only pending events under a tail end vouched for by a note signed with the tail's key and kept beside the head note (locks/<tail>.head.sig: seq, hash, prev, the signature coverage and the last checkpoint's hash), after recomputing the entry hash and the link of every pending event; the note is verified with the writer's key in memory, never a public key from the tree; an end the note does not vouch for, with pending events, goes to a new tail; no kind or field of the record changes and nothing migrates

payload.alternatives: Provocative tone: mnema has a thesis it could defend head-on, but in a loud category it reads as more noise. Polished standard: the generic SaaS look of the current site. Editorial restrained: safe, and close to the cream-and-serif look the AI companies now share. Authority: fits 'proof' but slides into preaching. Functional or merely considered ambition: what produced the sterile symbols.
payload.rationale: The identity work (ADR-370) lacked a shared brief, and the symbols it produced were correct but sterile. The four-axis brief fixes the gravitational centre every later choice answers to. Professional: the AI-tool category is loud, so restraint in the words is what differs. Controlled maximalism: high density where every element is intentional, which is the drawing sheet of direction B (zones, dimensions, title block, revision table, strike-through) the maintainer liked, and where the creative part can live. Peer: developers addressed in their own vocabulary, without preaching. Resonant: the reader should feel something the brand architected, which is what the maintainer asked for when he said the symbols had no creative part.
payload.title: mnema's aesthetic brief sits on four axes: a professional tone, controlled maximalism (the drawing-sheet language of direction B), a peer relationship with the reader, and a resonant sensory ambition

payload.alternatives: The drawing-sheet language of direction B (ADR-405): turned down for this one. A typographic identity on six posts and an editorial palette: reads as a magazine, and its symbol becomes three bars at 16 px. A faceless needle and a red thread: weakest at 16 px, reads as a sewing brand. An ochre iris on light grounds: a second colour for the eye. A realistic iris with a glint: reads as a camera lens.
payload.rationale: ADR-370 asked for the identity to be redone on every surface. The maintainer compared three complete directions and chose this one; the field and the fixed point say what the product does (the work moves around what was settled), and the eye is the witness that checks, which the README's verify promises. A market study found no eye among memory, provenance or decision-record tools, yellow on near-black already held by several developer tools as a button colour, and a surveillance reading driven by a realistic iris with a glint; hence a flat iris, yellow kept for meaning, and the eye still everywhere but the two surfaces where a person arrives.
payload.title: mnema's visual identity is the field of lines and the eye: work drawn as parallel lines, a decision as a fixed point the lines part around, the point drawn as an almond eye with a flat sulphur-yellow iris (no glint, no pupil, never a camera lens) that looks around and blinks only on the README banner and the site; charcoal #131312, bone #efebe1, paper #f6f3ec, stone #8c8a82; the light mode is the dark one inverted, the iris keeping its yellow with a thin charcoal ring; yellow only where it means something (the iris, a decision in force, a record verified), charcoal and weight elsewhere on light grounds

payload.alternatives: The lettering as first drawn: spurs and pointed corners. Striped letters cut by the field's lines: busy, close to a well-known striped logo. Wide capitals with the eye in the A: generic. The word on a line of the field: reads as underlined text. A type designer's pass before production: the maintainer chose this refinement instead.
payload.rationale: Drawn from the symbol, so the eye and the word read as one family; refined by the maintainer's request (no spurs at the stem tops, no pointed corners) and corrected after an audit measured the almonds floating above the baseline and uneven contacts between letters. Other products named Mnema and Mneme exist in the same space, so the lettering travels with the descriptor.
payload.title: The wordmark is "Pálpebra": lowercase mnema drawn as one line, the arches of m and n as upper lids widening from their stems, the bowls of e and a as almonds overshooting the x-height and the baseline by 1.3 units with round corners, stems standing on the baseline, edge-to-edge spacing; it always appears with the descriptor "the decision record for AI coding agents", the eye alone being used only as an avatar or an icon

payload.rationale: A probe on main 34fe5138 confirmed two open doors in the switch that is the person's only brake on agent acceptances: with agent-accepts off, an agent took a person-accepted decision out of force by superseding it with a merely proposed successor (CLI and MCP alike), and an agent with no terminal ran `mnema switch on agent-accepts` and then accepted as an agent. Taking a rule out of force carries the same weight as putting one in force, so the same seat rule (no declared agent and a pair of TTYs) applies to both; and a brake the braked party can release is no brake. Turning the switch off only tightens, so it stays open to an agent. The seat is the heuristic the product already declares in docs/what-it-proves.md; nothing new is recorded.
payload.title: With agent-accepts off, superseding a decision is a person's act like accepting one, and switching agent-accepts back on needs a person at a terminal; switching it off stays free to anyone

payload.rationale: A probe over 199 outside ADRs imported 197 and refused 2 (one with no Context, one with a field above 64 KiB): an import that refuses a real team's ADR stops the import of their history. The body by its author's headings keeps their words without guessing which section is the why; the cut keeps the 64 KiB field limit of the format untouched, and the hash with the derived-from link lets anyone check the whole text; running the credential check on the whole text first means the cut never hides a secret past the check.

GitHub through gh is the only forge the project verifies; refusing elsewhere with the manual step keeps ADR-145's forge-neutral path. payload.alternatives: Links in a second append after the decision: a refused link would leave the decision recorded without its paths. A new lock or a new kind: the item asked for no format change. The path rule is the one mnema link --rel governs already applies (governsTargets in link-target.ts).

A maintainer's choice and a manual assignment are acts of a person and are left alone. A marker copied by a stranger must not suppress a reply.

payload.alternatives: A flag on verify: verify must never change its exit. Identity by regular expression (cosign's --certificate-identity-regexp): easy to widen by mistake; can come later if asked. Passing when no bundle exists: an empty check would read as a confirmed witness.
payload.rationale: verify promises never to change its exit code, and a third party checking a countersignature needs an exit of its own. Exact identity and issuer, as cosign does, leave no regular expression to widen by mistake. A record with no bundle passing as checked would say the witness was confirmed when nothing was there. Writing the message and the cosign line lets the same bundle be checked by a tool mnema does not ship.
payload.title: The outside witness is checked against an expected signer by a new verb, mnema witness sigstore-check, with --identity and --issuer required and compared exactly; it fails when no bundle exists, refuses --json, and can write each checkpoint's message with the matching cosign verify-blob line

payload.alternatives: A Merkle inclusion path: the chain is linear, there is none. Carrying whole tail prefixes: almost the whole repository. Only the enrolment chain down to the signer: would hide a later revocation. Trusting the manifest or carrying none: a changed word could pass. A verify --proof flag: changes what verify promises. An MCP tool now: left for later. Carrying an .ots witness or the full checkpoint prev chain: later.
payload.rationale: A third party should be able to check one decision without the whole repository, using the record's own signed bytes and both readers' existing code paths. A content root folds a whole range, so ranges travel whole; the roster must fold the same over the file as over the record so a revocation is not hidden; the manifest is only a claim so one changed word fails. The proof states its own limits: nothing after the last range, nothing on a tail not carried, no time but the writer's clock, not who held a key.
payload.title: mnema prove <decision> writes one canonical JSON file under a new scheme, mnema-proof/1 (FORMAT.md section 9): the whole signed checkpoint ranges that hold the decision's writes and moves (and a superseding decision's birth), the roster facts of every identity those lines name until the set stops growing, tail proofs, public keys and a manifest that both checkers derive from the lines and refuse on any difference; no new signature; mnema prove --check <file> and the Python reader verify it and print the four things it does not prove

payload.alternatives: Words inside the session journal: mixes the person's text into a file read for other purposes. One verb per host: duplicates the table. Wiring the hooks now: conflicts with #1381 in the generated hooks files.
payload.rationale: ADR-658 asks for the words where no transcript reader exists; one verb and one host table (WORDS_HOOKS) keep it host-agnostic (ADR-656). Keeping the words in their own file leaves the journal free of the person's text and lets each be pruned and permissioned on its own. Wiring the hooks files in the same PR as #1381 would make two PRs fight over generated files.
payload.title: The person's words are kept by one read verb, mnema words --host <host>, called by each host's prompt hook (marked typed) and after-a-question hook (marked chosen, decided by the payload carrying tool_name), in a per-session file beside the session journal (<session>.words.jsonl, never inside it); the answers extractor is one tolerant reader shared by every host (answers, llmContent JSON, metadata.answers); the hooks files are wired only after #1381 lands, since both touch them

payload.alternatives: Keep gaps, refuse a carried move that is not applied and print a fifth non-claim that what lies between ranges is not covered: keeps files small (about 10 KB here) but a revocation omitted between ranges stays undetected.
payload.rationale: The review of #1441 proved an omission attack in both checkers: dropping the range where the superseding decision was born made a superseded decision read as accepted (VERIFIED in Python 3.9 and 3.12, PROVEN accepted in TypeScript); a key revocation or a retraction between two carried ranges could be hidden the same way, and an honest prover's gaps were indistinguishable from a malicious one's. What serves the proof wins over a small file.
payload.title: A proof of one decision (mnema-proof/1) carries no gap: on every tail it carries, every checkpoint range from the first carried range to the last goes in the file, and both checkers refuse a file with a gap between two carried ranges of one tail

payload.alternatives: Keep string compare and only validate the format: the exclusive --to day stays surprising. Read a zone-less timestamp in local time: the same command would select different records on different machines. payload.rationale: The window compared raw strings, so --to garbage silently returned everything. Parsing once at the door gives one answer for every reader. A date's natural reading as an upper bound is "up to the end of that day"; the old string compare excluded the day. A timestamp without a zone would name a different instant on each machine.
payload.title: A date window (--from/--to, and from/to in the MCP search and audit_accountability tools) is parsed at the door as YYYY-MM-DD (UTC) or an ISO timestamp with Z or ±HH:MM, normalised to the stored form, and anything else is refused naming the flag or field; a date in --to covers the whole UTC day and a date in --from starts it; a timestamp without a zone is refused
